retrofit: msg-message-queues: bare 'fanout' in the RabbitMQ exchange list linked to SD/05 gossip fanout; reworded to name the four exchange types and added a 'fanout-exchange' glossary entry.
retrofit: msg-ordering-backpressure: full-jitter block now states that AWS writes the exponent as the attempt count while here n counts retries from 1 (exponent n − 1).
retrofit: glossary absolute-state: removed alias 'absolute value' (mislinked the maths meaning).
retrofit: glossary stateful-operator: definition rewritten (was a broad 'depending on remembered information' gloss).
retrofit: glossary kappa-architecture: definition and source now Jay Kreps' 2014 O'Reilly article instead of the Lambda architecture Wikipedia page.
retrofit: glossary pane: definition sourced to Li et al. 2005 ('No pane, no gain') and notes the different Apache Beam meaning.
retrofit: glossary accumulation-mode: definition clarified; bare aliases 'accumulating', 'discarding', 'retracting', 'retraction' removed.
retrofit: glossary aws-lambda: '15 minutes' now qualified as a standard function's maximum (900 s); Lambda Managed Instances allow longer.
retrofit: glossary throttling: definition broadened to cover limiting a process's work (OS usage).

retrofit: glossary aliases that captured other meanings removed or qualified: offset(s), socket(s), zombie(s)/fenced, epoch(s), sink(s), salting/salted/sub-key(s), replay*, topic(s), exchanges, decoupl*, savepoint(s), projection(s), watermark(s), grace period, checkpoint*, changelog(s), lag/time lag, FIFO queue(s), keyed by/on, message key, at most once, point-to-point, global order, windowed, stateful processing, upcast, event messages, command handlers, deltas, log replay, subscriber(s), Publisher; terms renamed with qualifiers and lessons reworded so first mentions still link.
retrofit: glossary sql-delete renamed 'SQL DELETE' so SD/07's HTTP DELETE no longer links to it.

lowConfidence.claim: glossary processing-time keeps the bare alias 'Processing time'
lowConfidence.reason: Networks lessons use 'server processing time' (a duration) 4 times without their own entry, so those fall back to this stream-processing definition; left because the lesson bolds the bare phrase.
Other subjects use 'backlog' (TCP listen backlog, work backlog); the generic 'work waiting to be processed' meaning fits most uses but not a Scrum product backlog.

gaps: Every paragraph and every question field was read. Core semantics primary-source checked, but no complete separate source ledger for every original assertion; module confidence medium. claimsChecked counts enumerated correction groups conservatively.

Two Python fences executed (one uses application adapters); four JSON fences parsed; eleven numerical assertions and three SQL examples with duplicate/stale replay assertions passed on isolated PostgreSQL18. Java Kafka/Flink snippets and temporal-join SQL were API/documentation reviewed, not executed in full framework clusters. Ellipsis SQL outbox/offset examples are schematic rather than executable programs.

No live AWS/Google Cloud calls, distributed broker failover experiments, Flink checkpoint recovery, Kafka transaction fencing, production throughput benchmarks or hardware fault tests. Current product facts checked against cited official documentation; limits/settings remain version and deployment dependent.

No deployment-specific legal compliance determination for crypto-shredding; that conclusion is explicitly absent in lesson and question. Key destruction depends on copies, backups, caching and provider deletion lifecycle.
Reference URLs were checked selectively for claims; the inherited link collection was not exhaustively fetched by this child pass. Root runs project integration/link checks.
